accepted.label: Monte Carlo Simulation for Risk Assessment
accepted.description: Stochastic modeling uses probability distributions to simulate risk factors, generating a full distribution of outcomes rather than a single point estimate, enabling more informed decision-making.
coverage_criteria: Explain how Monte Carlo simulation differs from deterministic modeling, and describe the steps: defining distributions, running iterations, and interpreting a frequency histogram of outcomes.
accepted.merge_rationale: Both candidates describe the fundamental difference between deterministic and stochastic approaches and the core Monte Carlo method; they together form one teachable concept.

accepted.label: Sensitivity Analysis to Identify Key Risk Factors
accepted.description: Sensitivity analysis uses tornado graphs and spider charts to rank risk factors by their impact on the output criterion, helping prioritize factors for risk management.
coverage_criteria: Interpret a tornado graph: identify the factor with the widest bar, explain quantile ranges, and determine direction of impact.
accepted.merge_rationale: This candidate provides a focused method for analyzing which inputs most affect simulation outputs.

accepted.label: Risk Mapping for Preliminary Risk Identification
accepted.description: Risk mapping uses expert assessment to score probability and impact, creating a matrix that categorizes risks to guide quantitative analysis.
coverage_criteria: Create a risk matrix given a list of risks, assign probability and impact scores, and explain how the matrix informs subsequent simulation focus.
accepted.merge_rationale: This candidate introduces a qualitative step that precedes simulation, identifying which risks are worth modeling.

accepted.label: Project Comparison Using Simulation Statistics
accepted.description: When comparing projects using simulation results, apply decision rules based on mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, and skewness to select the best project.
coverage_criteria: Compare two projects using mean, standard deviation, and skewness; explain which project is preferable and why; compute and interpret the coefficient of variation.
accepted.merge_rationale: This candidate directly addresses how to translate simulation outputs into a business recommendation by comparing projects.
